title: Cut generated commit subjects at a word boundary, not mid-word
summary: Generated commit subjects and titles are cut with `.chars().take(72)` at several sites (manage.rs intervention subject, reading.rs title, store.rs title fallback), leaving fragments like "…tells outsi" (review n4). I'll add one shared word-boundary truncation helper and use it at those sites, so Athena's maintainers see whole words in `git log`.

defaults_applied.how: One shared helper replaces every fixed-width subject/title cut.
Unit tests for the helper; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Criteria check cut output, not that the helper exists.
Verifier runs cargo test, clippy, fmt --check.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: commit subjects (and the titles that feed them via closing_subject) never end mid-word; audience is maintainers reading git log.
Limit stays 72 characters; if the text fits it is unchanged.
A single word longer than the limit falls back to a hard cut at the limit.
Fix is a shared helper (likely in commits.rs) used by every take(72) subject/title site, per root-cause; reading.rs:553 (take(60)) is checked and converted if it also feeds a subject.
No ellipsis is added unless the existing behavior had one; it had none.

acceptance_criteria.text: Unit tests for the new helper pass (`cargo test`): text over 72 chars is cut at the last whitespace so no word is split; text under the limit is unchanged; a single over-long word is hard-cut; multibyte characters do not panic.
A test that builds a long intervention subject and a long reading title shows neither ends mid-word and both are ≤72 chars (`cargo test`).
manage.rs, reading.rs and store.rs no longer use a bare `.chars().take(72)` for subjects/titles; they call the shared helper.
`cargo clippy` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes.
CHANGELOG.md notes that generated commit subjects are cut at word boundaries.

out_of_scope: Other n-items in the review (n3, n5)
Truncations that are not commit subjects or titles (jev.rs, introspect.rs, audience.rs page caps)
